1:1.sourceText: Παῦλος ἀπόστολος, οὐκ ἀπ’ ἀνθρώπων οὐδὲ δι’ ἀνθρώπου ἀλλὰ διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς τοῦ ἐγείραντος αὐτὸν ἐκ νεκρῶν,
1:1.targetText: Paul, an apostle—not from men, nor through man, but through Jesus Christ, and God the Father, who raised Him out of the dead—

1:2.sourceText: καὶ οἱ σὺν ἐμοὶ πάντες ἀδελφοί, ταῖς ἐκκλησίαις τῆς Γαλατίας·
1:2.targetText: and all the brothers with me, to the assemblies of Galatia:

1:3.sourceText: χάρις ὑμῖν καὶ εἰρήνη ἀπὸ Θεοῦ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν καὶ Κυρίου Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ,
1:3.targetText: Grace to you and peace from God the Father and our Lord Jesus Christ,

groups.note: Pinned N1904 places ἡμῶν with Father; LSV places the English our with Lord. The same first-person plural possessors are retained with the changed placement/head explicit; no extra possessive is invented.

1:4.sourceText: τοῦ δόντος ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν, ὅπως ἐξέληται ἡμᾶς ἐκ τοῦ αἰῶνος τοῦ ἐνεστῶτος πονηροῦ κατὰ τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς ἡμῶν,
1:4.targetText: who gave Himself for our sins, that He might deliver us out of the present evil age, according to the will of our God and Father,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

1:5.sourceText: ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων· ἀμήν.
1:5.targetText: to whom [is] the glory through the ages of the ages. Amen.

groups.note: Greek εἰς introduces the temporal duration for the ages; LSV renders that relation through. This is a contextual duration correspondence, not a general assertion that εἰς means through.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English copula supplied in the glory doxology.

1:6.sourceText: Θαυμάζω ὅτι οὕτως ταχέως μετατίθεσθε ἀπὸ τοῦ καλέσαντος ὑμᾶς ἐν χάριτι Χριστοῦ εἰς ἕτερον εὐαγγέλιον,
1:6.targetText: I wonder that you are so quickly removed from Him who called you in the grace of Christ to another good news—

1:7.sourceText: ὃ οὐκ ἔστιν ἄλλο· εἰ μή τινές εἰσιν οἱ ταράσσοντες ὑμᾶς καὶ θέλοντες μεταστρέψαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1:7.targetText: not that there is another, except there are certain who are troubling you, and wishing to pervert the good news of the Christ;

groups.note: The Greek relative which introduces the no-other-gospel qualification; LSV expresses it as not that there is another. The shared referential qualification is retained through the changed English clause form.

1:8.sourceText: ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐὰν ἡμεῖς ἢ ἄγγελος ἐξ οὐρανοῦ εὐαγγελίσηται ὑμῖν παρ’ ὃ εὐηγγελισάμεθα ὑμῖν, ἀνάθεμα ἔστω.
1:8.targetText: but even if we or a messenger out of Heaven may proclaim good news to you different from what we proclaimed to you—let him be accursed!

1:9.sourceText: ὡς προειρήκαμεν, καὶ ἄρτι πάλιν λέγω, εἴ τις ὑμᾶς εὐαγγελίζεται παρ’ ὃ παρελάβετε, ἀνάθεμα ἔστω.
1:9.targetText: As we have said before, and now say again: if anyone may proclaim to you good news different from what you received—let him be accursed!

groups.note: The Greek λέγω is first-person singular I say; LSV leaves the subject implicit after the earlier we-have-said clause. The actual saying verb is linked without manufacturing a second English I.

1:10.sourceText: Ἄρτι γὰρ ἀνθρώπους πείθω ἢ τὸν Θεόν; ἢ ζητῶ ἀνθρώποις ἀρέσκειν; εἰ ἔτι ἀνθρώποις ἤρεσκον, Χριστοῦ δοῦλος οὐκ ἂν ἤμην.
1:10.targetText: For do I now persuade men, or God? Or do I seek to please men? For if I yet pleased men—I should not be Christ’s servant.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective difference: LSV follows the additional γάρ with the final if-clause; pinned N1904 has no separate explanatory particle at that point.

1:11.sourceText: γνωρίζω γὰρ ὑμῖν, ἀδελφοί, τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τὸ εὐαγγελισθὲν ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ ὅτι οὐκ ἔστιν κατὰ ἄνθρωπον·
1:11.targetText: And I make known to you, brothers, the good news that was proclaimed by me, that it is not according to man,

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness connective difference: pinned N1904 has γάρ, for, whereas LSV follows δέ, And.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness connective difference: LSV follows δέ rather than the γάρ written in pinned N1904.

1:12.sourceText: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐγὼ παρὰ ἀνθρώπου παρέλαβον αὐτό οὔτε ἐδιδάχθην, ἀλλὰ δι’ ἀποκαλύψεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ.
1:12.targetText: for neither did I receive it from man, nor was I taught [it], but through a revelation of Jesus Christ,

groups.note: The one written αὐτό is the gospel object received and understood with the coordinated taught predicate. LSV repeats that same object in brackets; both mentions retain the actual shared original pronoun.

1:13.sourceText: Ἠκούσατε γὰρ τὴν ἐμὴν ἀναστροφήν ποτε ἐν τῷ Ἰουδαϊσμῷ, ὅτι καθ’ ὑπερβολὴν ἐδίωκον τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ καὶ ἐπόρθουν αὐτήν,
1:13.targetText: for you heard of my behavior once in Judaism, that I was exceedingly persecuting the Assembly of God, and destroying it,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

1:14.sourceText: καὶ προέκοπτον ἐν τῷ Ἰουδαϊσμῷ ὑπὲρ πολλοὺς συνηλικιώτας ἐν τῷ γένει μου, περισσοτέρως ζηλωτὴς ὑπάρχων τῶν πατρικῶν μου παραδόσεων.
1:14.targetText: and I was advancing in Judaism above many equals in age in my own race, being more abundantly zealous of my fathers’ deliverances,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds an ownership emphasis with my race; no separate Greek own adjective is written.

1:15.sourceText: Ὅτε δὲ εὐδόκησεν ὁ ἀφορίσας με ἐκ κοιλίας μητρός μου καὶ καλέσας διὰ τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ
1:15.targetText: and when God was well pleased—having separated me from the womb of my mother, and having called [me] through His grace—

groups.note: The written με is the object of separated and is understood with the coordinated called participle. English repeats me in brackets for the second predicate; both mentions refer to this same actual original object.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

N1904 substantivizes the separating participle with ὁ, the one who separated. LSV follows the longer explicit God-subject wording and renders the participle having separated, without an English article or the-one phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: Source-witness subject difference: LSV explicitly names God here; pinned N1904 has the substantivized the-one-who-separated expression without a written Θεός.

1:16.sourceText: ἀποκαλύψαι τὸν Υἱὸν αὐτοῦ ἐν ἐμοὶ, ἵνα εὐαγγελίζωμαι αὐτὸν ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, εὐθέως οὐ προσανεθέμην σαρκὶ καὶ αἵματι,
1:16.targetText: to reveal His Son in me, that I might proclaim Him as good news among the nations, I did not immediately confer with flesh and blood,

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article is not separately expressed in this English possessive, personal-name or noun construction.

1:17.sourceText: οὐδὲ ἀνῆλθον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα πρὸς τοὺς πρὸ ἐμοῦ ἀποστόλους, ἀλλὰ ἀπῆλθον εἰς Ἀραβίαν, καὶ πάλιν ὑπέστρεψα εἰς Δαμασκόν.
1:17.targetText: nor did I go up to Jerusalem to those who were apostles before me, but I went away to Arabia, and again returned to Damascus;

groups.note: The Greek substantival apostles noun phrase is expanded by English into those who were apostles. The full nominal constituent is retained without assigning the past auxiliary were to an isolated article.

1:18.sourceText: Ἔπειτα μετὰ τρία ἔτη ἀνῆλθον εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἱστορῆσαι Κηφᾶν, καὶ ἐπέμεινα πρὸς αὐτὸν ἡμέρας δεκαπέντε·
1:18.targetText: then, after three years I went up to Jerusalem to inquire about Peter, and remained with him fifteen days,

groups.note: N1904 names Κηφᾶν, Cephas, while LSV uses Peter. These are the Aramaic and Greek names of the same person, explicitly identified together in John 1:42. The actual Greek Cephas identity is preserved; it is not silently relabeled as the Πέτρος lexeme.

1:19.sourceText: ἕτερον δὲ τῶν ἀποστόλων οὐκ εἶδον, εἰ μὴ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν τοῦ Κυρίου.
1:19.targetText: and I did not see [any] other of the apostles, except James, the brother of the LORD.

unmappedTarget.reason: Bracketed English indefinite supplement supplied before other; no separate corresponding Greek word is written.

1:20.sourceText: ἃ δὲ γράφω ὑμῖν, ἰδοὺ ἐνώπιον τοῦ Θεοῦ ὅτι οὐ ψεύδομαι.
1:20.targetText: And the things that I write to you, behold, before God—I do not lie;

Greek ὅτι introduces the solemn assurance; English proceeds directly to I do not lie without a separate that.

1:23.targetText: and they were only hearing that “he who is persecuting us then, now proclaims good news—the faith that he was then destroying”;

1:24.sourceText: καὶ ἐδόξαζον ἐν ἐμοὶ τὸν Θεόν.
